metadata.title: On the existence of asymptotically good linear codes in minor-closed classes

extraction_notes.note: Section 2 restates in matroid language that the class of all F-represented matroids is asymptotically good; treated as a repeat of the introduction's statement for codes (ClP1) and given no node of its own.
Kashyap's cited result is stated only inside the sentence saying Theorem 1.2 generalises it; the whole sentence is the node, so it also carries the paper's comparison.
One- or two-sentence justifications leading into Lemma 2.3, Lemma 4.1 and Theorem 1.1 were emitted as prose proof nodes rather than as standalone claims.
Abstract's definition of asymptotically good sequences of codes, the Section 4 repeat of the F_prime notation, and the Section 5 reminder that a cycle is an edge set are repeats and got no node.
The whole argument rests on the Geelen-Gerards-Whittle structure theorem, whose proof the paper says is unpublished; TP4 is kept as an external result.

nodes.name: Prime subfield $\mathbb{F}_{\mathrm{prime}}$
nodes.statement: For a finite field $\mathbb F$, let $\mathbb{F}_{\mathrm{prime}}$ denote the unique subfield of $\mathbb F$ of prime order.

nodes.name: Code parameters $n_C$, $k_C$, $d_C$
nodes.statement: For a linear code $C$, denote the length of $C$ by $n_C$, the dimension of $C$ by $k_C$, and the minimum Hamming distance of $C$ by $d_C$.

nodes.name: $[n,k,d]$ code
nodes.statement: In short, $C$ is an $[n_C, k_C, d_C]$ code.

nodes.name: Asymptotically good class of codes
nodes.statement: A class $\mathcal{C}$ of codes is \emph{asymptotically good} if there exists $\varepsilon > 0$ such that for every $n \in \mathbb Z^+$ there is a code $C \in \mathcal{C}$ of length $n_C \geq n$ satisfying $k_C \ge \varepsilon n_C$ and $d_C \ge \varepsilon n_C$.
differentia: there exists $\varepsilon > 0$ such that for every $n \in \mathbb Z^+$ there is a code $C \in \mathcal{C}$ of length $n_C \geq n$ satisfying $k_C \ge \varepsilon n_C$ and $d_C \ge \varepsilon n_C$
nodes.statement_short: A class of codes is asymptotically good if it has arbitrarily long codes with rate and relative distance both at least some fixed $\varepsilon>0$.

nodes.name: Linear codes over a finite field are asymptotically good
nodes.statement: For every finite field $\mathbb F$, the class of linear codes over $\mathbb F$ is asymptotically good, as suitable random codes have nonvanishing rate and minimum distance.
assumptions: For every finite field $\mathbb F$
conclusions: the class of linear codes over $\mathbb F$ is asymptotically good

nodes.name: Puncturing
nodes.statement: Given a code $C$, the \emph{puncturing} of $C$ at $i$ is the code obtained from $C$ by removing the $i$th coordinate from each word.
differentia: by removing the $i$th coordinate from each word

nodes.name: Shortening
nodes.statement: The \emph{shortening} of $C$ at $i$ is the code obtained from $C$ by selecting only the codewords of $C$ having a $0$ in position $i$, and then puncturing the resulting code at $i$.
differentia: selecting only the codewords of $C$ having a $0$ in position $i$, and then puncturing the resulting code at $i$

nodes.name: Main theorem: asymptotically good code classes contain all prime-field codes as minors
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbb F$ be a finite field. If $\mathcal{C}$ is an asymptotically good class of linear codes over $\mathbb F$, then every linear code $C'$ over $\mathbb{F}_{\mathrm{prime}}$ can be obtained from a code $C \in \mathcal{C}$ by a sequence of puncturings and shortenings.
assumptions: Let $\mathbb F$ be a finite field.
$\mathcal{C}$ is an asymptotically good class of linear codes over $\mathbb F$
conclusions: every linear code $C'$ over $\mathbb{F}_{\mathrm{prime}}$ can be obtained from a code $C \in \mathcal{C}$ by a sequence of puncturings and shortenings
nodes.statement_short: Every asymptotically good class of $\mathbb F$-linear codes yields every $\mathbb{F}_{\mathrm{prime}}$-linear code via puncturing and shortening.
nodes.label: main

nodes.name: Proper puncture/shorten-closed classes over prime fields are not asymptotically good
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbb F$ be a field of prime order. If $\mathcal{C}$ is a proper subclass of the linear codes over $\mathbb F$ that is closed under puncturing and shortening, then $\mathcal{C}$ is not asymptotically good.
assumptions: Let $\mathbb F$ be a field of prime order.
$\mathcal{C}$ is a proper subclass of the linear codes over $\mathbb F$ that is closed under puncturing and shortening
conclusions: $\mathcal{C}$ is not asymptotically good

nodes.name: Kashyap: graphic and almost-graphic binary codes are not asymptotically good
nodes.statement: When $|\mathbb F| = 2$, this substantially generalises results of Kashyap [\ref{kashyap}] which show that the classes of graphic binary codes, as well as a slightly larger class of `almost-graphic' codes, are not asymptotically good.
assumptions: When $|\mathbb F| = 2$
conclusions: the classes of graphic binary codes, as well as a slightly larger class of `almost-graphic' codes, are not asymptotically good

nodes.name: $\mathbb F$-represented matroid
nodes.statement: If $\mathbb F$ is a field, then an \emph{$\mathbb F$-represented matroid} is a pair $M = (E,U)$, where $E$ is a finite set and $U$ is a subspace of $\mathbb F^E$.

nodes.name: Size $|M|$
nodes.statement: We write $|M|$ for $|E|$.

nodes.name: Generator matrix $M(A)$
nodes.statement: If $A$ is an $\mathbb F$-matrix with column set $E$ such that $\mathrm{rowspace}(A) = U$, then we write $M = M(A)$; we call $A$ a \emph{generator matrix} for $M$ and say that $A$ \emph{generates} $M$.

nodes.name: Restriction and rank $r_M(X)$
nodes.statement: For $X \subseteq E$ we write $u|X$ for the restriction of the vector $u$ to those coordinates indexed by $X$, we write $U|X$ for the space $\{u|X: u \in U\}$, and we write $r_M(X)$ for the dimension of $U|X$.

nodes.name: Rank $r(M)$
nodes.statement: We denote $r_M(E)$ simply by $r(M)$.

nodes.name: Rank function
nodes.statement: We call $r_M$ the \emph{rank function} of $M$.

nodes.name: Codes as represented matroids
nodes.statement: If $C$ is a $q$-ary $[n,k,d]$ code, then $M = (\{1,\ldots, n\}, C)$ is a matroid with $|M| = n$ and $r(M) = k$. The rank function simply gives the dimension of this code and of all its puncturings.
nodes.statement_short: A $q$-ary $[n,k,d]$ code is a represented matroid of size $n$ and rank $k$.

nodes.name: Projective equivalence
nodes.statement: We give a name to this equivalence: two $\mathbb F$-represented matroids $(E,U_1)$ and $(E,U_2)$ are \emph{projectively equivalent} if $U_2 = \{uD: u \in U_1\}$ for some nonsingular diagonal matrix $D$.

nodes.name: Dual matroid $M^*$
nodes.statement: The \emph{dual matroid} $M^*$ of an $\mathbb F$-represented matroid $M = (E,U)$ is defined to be $(E,U^{\perp})$, where $U^\perp$ denotes the orthogonal complement of $U$.

nodes.name: Deletion and contraction
nodes.statement: For $X \subseteq E$ we write $M \!\setminus\! X$ for $(E-X,U|(E-X))$ and $M / X$ for $(M^* \!\setminus\! X)^*$; these are the matroids obtained from $M$ by \emph{deletion} and \emph{contraction} of $X$ respectively; these operations correspond to puncturing and shortening of codes.

nodes.name: Minor
nodes.statement: If $N$ is an $\mathbb F$-represented matroid that is projectively equivalent to $M / C \!\setminus\! D$ for some disjoint subsets $C$ and $D$ of $E$, then we say $N$ is a \emph{minor} of $M$.

nodes.name: Minor-closed class
nodes.statement: A class $\mathcal{M}$ of matroids is \emph{minor-closed} if $\mathcal{M}$ is closed under taking minors and isomorphism.
differentia: closed under taking minors and isomorphism

nodes.name: Spanning and independent sets
nodes.statement: A set $X \subseteq E$ is \emph{spanning} in $M$ if $r_M(X) = r(M)$ and \emph{independent} in $M$ if $r_M(X) = |X|$.

nodes.name: Dependent set
nodes.statement: If $X$ is not independent then $X$ is \emph{dependent}.

nodes.name: Circuit and cocircuit
nodes.statement: A \emph{circuit} of $M$ is a minimal dependent set and a \emph{cocircuit} of $M$ is a minimal dependent set of $M^*$, or equivalently a minimal set $C$ satisfying $r(M \!\setminus\! C) < r(M)$.

nodes.name: Girth $g(M)$
nodes.statement: For a matroid $M$, we write $g(M)$ for the size of a smallest circuit of $M$, also called the \emph{girth} of $M$.
nodes.genus: size of a smallest circuit of $M$

nodes.name: Code minimum distance equals cogirth
nodes.statement: If $C$ is a $q$-ary $[n,k,d]$ code, then $M = (\{1,\ldots, n\}, C)$ is a matroid with $g(M^*) = d$.

nodes.name: $d(M)$
nodes.statement: For that reason we sometimes write $d(M)$ for $g(M^*)$.

nodes.name: Vertically $t$-connected matroid
nodes.statement: There are many notions of matroid connectivity but we just need one; for $t \in \mathbb Z^+$, a matroid $M = (E,U)$ is \emph{vertically $t$-connected} if, for every partition $(A,B)$ of $E$ satisfying $r_M(A) + r_M(B) < r(M) + t - 1$, either $A$ or $B$ is spanning in $M$.
differentia: for every partition $(A,B)$ of $E$ satisfying $r_M(A) + r_M(B) < r(M) + t - 1$, either $A$ or $B$ is spanning in $M$
nodes.statement_short: $M$ is vertically $t$-connected if every partition with low connectivity has a spanning side.

nodes.name: Vertical 2-connectivity versus direct sums
nodes.statement: For instance, $M$ is vertically 2-connected if and only if $M$ cannot be written as the direct sum of two positive-rank matroids.

nodes.name: $\mathbb F$-frame matrix and frame matroid
nodes.statement: An \emph{$\mathbb F$-frame matrix} is an $\mathbb F$-matrix in which every column has at most two nonzero entries, and an \emph{$\mathbb F$-represented frame matroid} is a matroid having an $\mathbb F$-frame matrix as a generator matrix.
differentia: every column has at most two nonzero entries

nodes.name: $\Gamma$-labelled digraph
nodes.statement: For a group $\Gamma$, a \emph{$\Gamma$-labelled digraph} is a pair $(G,\Sigma)$, where $G = (V,E)$ is a directed graph (allowing loops and multiple edges) and $\Sigma: E \to \Gamma$ is an assignment of a label in $\Gamma$ to every arc of $G$.

nodes.name: Graph representation of a frame matrix
nodes.statement: If $A$ is an $\mathbb F$-frame matrix with row set $V$ and column set $E$, then a \emph{graph representation} of $A$ is an $\mathbb F^{\times}$-labelled digraph $(G,\Sigma)$, where $G = (V,E)$ and $(G,\Sigma)$ satisfies the following conditions: \begin{itemize} \item If $A[e]$ has two nonzero entries in rows $x$ and $y$, then $e$ is an arc of $G$ from $x$ to $y$ with label $-A[e,x]A[e,y]^{-1}$ or an arc of $G$ from $y$ to $x$ with label $-A[e,y]A[e,x]^{-1}$, and \item If $A[e]$ has exactly one nonzero entry, then $e$ is a loop of $G$ at $x$ with arbitrary label in $\mathbb F^\times - \{1\}$. \item If $A[e] = 0$, then $e$ is a loop of $G$ with label $1$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: A graph representation of a frame matrix encodes each column as an arc (or loop) labelled by the ratio of its nonzero entries.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.1 (existence of small graph representations)
nodes.statement: It is clear that one frame matrix may have many graph representations, and that graph representations always exist unless $|\mathbb F| = 2$, where a frame matrix having a column with exactly one nonzero entry has no graph representations since $\mathbb F^{\times}-\{1\}$ is empty. However, appending a `parity' row to a binary frame matrix yields another row-equivalent frame matrix where every column has even support. Since we can remove redundant rows from an arbitrary frame matrix to still have a frame matrix and append a single row in this way in the binary case, we have the following statement, which we apply freely.
nodes.statement_short: Remove redundant rows; in the binary case append a parity row so every column has even support.

nodes.name: Existence of a graph representation with at most $r(M)+1$ rows
nodes.statement: If $M$ is an $\mathbb F$-represented frame matroid, then there is a generator matrix $A$ of $M$ having a graph representation and at most $r(M) + 1$ rows.
assumptions: $M$ is an $\mathbb F$-represented frame matroid
conclusions: there is a generator matrix $A$ of $M$ having a graph representation and at most $r(M) + 1$ rows
nodes.label: frameexist

nodes.name: Cycle and path of a digraph
nodes.statement: A \emph{cycle} or \emph{path} of a digraph $G$ will denote any cycle or path of the underlying undirected graph of $G$.

nodes.name: Sign of a cycle
nodes.statement: Let $C$ be a cycle of $G$, and $v_1,e_1,v_2,e_2,\dotsc,e_{k-1},v_k=v_1$ be a corresponding alternating sequence of vertices and arcs of $G$ (there are two choices for this sequence). Let $C^+$ be the set of $e_i$ such that $e_i$ is directed from $v_i$ to $v_{i+1}$ in $G$, and $C^-$ be the set of all other $e_i$. The \emph{sign} of $C$ (relative to this sequence) is $\prod_{e \in C^+} \Sigma(e) \prod_{e\in C^-} \Sigma(e)^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_short: The sign of a cycle is the product of its arc labels, inverting labels of arcs traversed backwards.

nodes.name: Balanced cycle
nodes.statement: We say that $C$ is a \emph{balanced} cycle of $(G,\Sigma)$ if $\mathrm{sign}(C) = 1$.

nodes.name: Balancedness is independent of traversal
nodes.statement: Note that a cycle being balanced does not depend on the choice of sequence of vertices and edges.
conclusions: a cycle being balanced does not depend on the choice of sequence of vertices and edges

nodes.name: Justification of Proposition 2.2
nodes.statement: There is a well-known characterisation of the set of circuits of $M(A)$ in terms of the balanced and unbalanced cycles of $(G,\Sigma)$, but we will just use the following weaker statement, which is fairly straightforward to check by considering linear dependencies in the columns of $A[C]$.
nodes.statement_short: Check directly via linear dependencies among the columns of $A[C]$.

nodes.name: Balanced cycles and bicycles are dependent
nodes.statement: If $(G,\Sigma)$ is a graph representation of an $\mathbb F$-frame matrix $A$ and $C$ is a balanced cycle of $(G,\Sigma)$ or a connected subgraph of $G$ of minimum degree 2 which is not a cycle of $G$, then $C$ is dependent in $M(A)$.
assumptions: $(G,\Sigma)$ is a graph representation of an $\mathbb F$-frame matrix $A$
$C$ is a balanced cycle of $(G,\Sigma)$ or a connected subgraph of $G$ of minimum degree 2 which is not a cycle of $G$
conclusions: $C$ is dependent in $M(A)$
nodes.label: bicycledependent

nodes.name: Resigning
nodes.statement: We say $(G, \Sigma')$ was obtained from $(G, \Sigma)$ by \emph{resigning} if, for some $\gamma \in \Gamma$ and for some partition $(U,W)$ of the vertices of $G$, we have \begin{align*} \Sigma'(e) = \begin{cases} \gamma \Sigma(e) & \text{ if } e \text{ runs from } U \text{ to } W;\\ \gamma^{-1} \Sigma(e) & \text{ if } e \text{ runs from } W \text{ to } U;\\ \Sigma(e) & \text{ otherwise}. \end{cases} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Resigning multiplies labels of arcs crossing a vertex partition $(U,W)$ by $\gamma^{\pm1}$ according to direction.

nodes.name: Resigning preserves balanced cycles
nodes.statement: It is easily checked that $(G, \Sigma)$ and $(G, \Sigma')$ have the same collection of balanced cycles.
conclusions: $(G, \Sigma)$ and $(G, \Sigma')$ have the same collection of balanced cycles

nodes.name: Resigning as row scaling
nodes.statement: In the representation this corresponds to scaling the rows indexed by $W$ by a factor $\gamma$.

nodes.name: Connected graph representation
nodes.statement: In what follows, we need to assume that the graph representation of a frame matroid is connected, which means that there is a path between every pair of vertices.

nodes.name: Justification of Lemma 2.3
nodes.statement: It is easy to show that a vertically $3$-connected matroid, with no elements $e$ such that $r_M(e) = 0$, has the property that every pair of elements is in a circuit. A consequence of this is:
nodes.statement_short: Every pair of elements of a loopless vertically 3-connected matroid lies in a circuit, forcing the graph to be connected.

nodes.name: Graph of a vertically 3-connected frame matroid is connected
nodes.statement: Let $(G,\Sigma)$ be a graph representation of an $\mathbb F$-represented frame matroid $M$. If $M$ is vertically 3-connected and has no loops, then $G$ is connected.
assumptions: Let $(G,\Sigma)$ be a graph representation of an $\mathbb F$-represented frame matroid $M$.
$M$ is vertically 3-connected and has no loops
conclusions: $G$ is connected
nodes.label: lem:graphconn

nodes.name: Vertically 3-connected frame matroids have connected graph representations
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be an $\mathbb F$-represented frame matroid. If $M$ is vertically 3-connected, then $M$ has a graph representation $(G,\Sigma)$ with $G$ connected.
assumptions: Let $M$ be an $\mathbb F$-represented frame matroid.
$M$ is vertically 3-connected
conclusions: $M$ has a graph representation $(G,\Sigma)$ with $G$ connected
nodes.label: cor:graphconn

nodes.name: $(\alpha,\beta)$-good sequence
nodes.statement: For $\alpha,\beta \in \mathbb R$ we say a sequence $M_0,M_1 \dotsc,$ of matroids is \emph{$(\alpha,\beta)$-good} if $|M_i| \ge i$, $r(M_i) \ge \alpha |M_i|$ and $g(M_i^*) \ge \beta|M_i|$ for each $i \in \mathbb Z_0^+$.

nodes.name: Asymptotically good class of matroids
nodes.statement: A class $\mathcal{M}$ of matroids is \emph{asymptotically good} if $\mathcal{M}$ contains an $(\alpha,\beta)$-good sequence for some $\alpha,\beta \in \mathbb R^+$.
differentia: $\mathcal{M}$ contains an $(\alpha,\beta)$-good sequence for some $\alpha,\beta \in \mathbb R^+$

nodes.name: Goodness parameters are at most 1
nodes.statement: Note that $\alpha,\beta \le 1$ for any such $\alpha,\beta$.
assumptions: for any such $\alpha,\beta$
conclusions: $\alpha,\beta \le 1$

nodes.name: Reduction to vertically $t$-connected matroids
nodes.statement: If $t \in \mathbb Z$ and $\mathcal{M}$ is an asymptotically good minor-closed class of matroids, then the class of vertically $t$-connected matroids in $\mathcal{M}$ is asymptotically good.
assumptions: $t \in \mathbb Z$
$\mathcal{M}$ is an asymptotically good minor-closed class of matroids
conclusions: the class of vertically $t$-connected matroids in $\mathcal{M}$ is asymptotically good
nodes.label: connreduction

nodes.name: Large terms of the good sequence are vertically $t$-connected
nodes.statement: For each $n \in \mathbb Z$ with $n \ge 2\beta^{-1}m$, the matroid $M_n$ is vertically $t$-connected.
assumptions: $n \in \mathbb Z$ with $n \ge 2\beta^{-1}m$
conclusions: the matroid $M_n$ is vertically $t$-connected

nodes.name: Proof of the claim in Lemma 3.1
nodes.statement: Suppose for a contradiction that $n \ge 2\beta^{-1}m$ and $M = M_n$ is not vertically $t$-connected. Let $(X_1,X_2)$ be a partition of $E(M)$ with $r_M(X_1) + r_M(X_2) = r(M) + t' - 1$ with $t' < t$ and $r_M(X_1),r_M(X_2) \ge t'$. Let $N_1 = M/ X_2$ and $N_2 = M / X_1$. Note that $N_1,N_2 \in \mathcal{M}$ and that $r(N_i) = r(M)-r_M(X_{3-i}) > r(M)-t+1$, so $r(N_1) + r(N_2) > r(M)-2t$. Since every cocircuit of $N_1$ or $N_2$ is a cocircuit of $M$, we have $g(M^*) \le \min(g(N_1^*),g(N_2^*))$.We have \[ \beta|M| \le g(M^*) \le \min(g(N_1^*),g(N_2^*)) \le \tfrac{1}{2}(g(N_1^*) + g(N_2^*))\] and, since $|M| = |N_1| + |N_2|$, we have either $g(N_1^*) \ge 2\beta|N_1|$ or $g(N_2^*) \ge 2\beta|N_2|$. We may assume that the first case holds. Since each of $X_1$ and $X_2$ contains a cocircuit of $M$, we have $|N_i| = |X_i| \ge g(M^*) \ge \beta|M| \ge m$ for each $i \in \{1,2\}$. Since $|N_1| + |N_2| = |M|$, this implies that $|N_1| \ge \tfrac{\beta}{1-\beta}|N_2|$. Moreover, $m \ge m_1$ gives $r(N_1) < \tfrac{1}{2}\alpha|N_1|$. We have \begin{align*} \alpha|M| &\le r(M) \\ &< r(N_1) + r(N_2) + 2t\\ &< \tfrac{1}{2}\alpha|N_1| + r(N_2) + 2t\\ &\le \tfrac{3}{4}\alpha|N_1| + r(N_2), \end{align*} Where the last line uses $\tfrac{1}{4}\alpha|N_1| \ge \tfrac{1}{4}\alpha m \ge 2t$. From this and $|M| = |N_1|+|N_2|$ we get \begin{align*} r(N_2) &\ge \tfrac{1}{4}\alpha|N_1| + \alpha|N_2|\\ &= \alpha\left(1 + \delta \right)|N_2| \end{align*} Now $|N_2| \ge m \ge m_2$ so $g(N_2^*) < \beta |N_2|$ by choice of $m_2$. However $g(M^*) \le g(N_2^*)$ and $\beta|N_2| < \beta|M|$, so $g(M^*) < \beta|M|$, contradicting the definition of $M$.
nodes.statement_short: Contradiction: a low-order separation splits $M_n$ into two contractions, one of which beats the extremal choice of $(\alpha,\beta)$.

nodes.name: Elementary projection and lift
nodes.statement: If $M_1 = (E,U_1)$ and $M_2 = (E,U_2)$ are $\mathbb F$-represented matroids and there is an $\mathbb F$-represented matroid $M$ with ground set $E \cup \{e\}$ satisfying $M \!\setminus\! e = M_1$ and $M / e = M_2$, then we say that $M_2$ is an \emph{elementary projection} of $M_1$ and $M_1$ is an \emph{elementary lift} of $M_2$.

nodes.name: Perturbation distance $\mathrm{dist}(M_1,M_2)$
nodes.statement: For arbitrary $\mathbb F$-represented matroids $M_1$ and $M_2$ on a common ground set $E$, we write $\mathrm{dist}(M_1,M_2)$ for the minimum number of elementary lifts/projections required to transform $M_1$ into $M_2$.

nodes.name: Distance is finite
nodes.statement: (It is clear that any matroid on $E$ can be transformed into the rank-$0$ matroid on $E$ by a finite sequence of projections, so this distance is always finite.)
conclusions: this distance is always finite

nodes.name: Distance via a single lift-projection matroid
nodes.statement: It is easy to see that, if $\mathrm{dist}(M_1,M_2) \le k$, then there is a matroid $M$ with ground set $E \cup C \cup D$ satisfying $M \!\setminus\! D / C = M_1$ and $M / D \!\setminus\! C = M_2$, where $|C|+|D| \le k$.
assumptions: $\mathrm{dist}(M_1,M_2) \le k$
conclusions: there is a matroid $M$ with ground set $E \cup C \cup D$ satisfying $M \!\setminus\! D / C = M_1$ and $M / D \!\setminus\! C = M_2$, where $|C|+|D| \le k$

nodes.name: Justification of Lemma 4.1
nodes.statement: Each elementary lift and projection can change the rank of a subset by at most one. From this we can deduce the following lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Each lift or projection changes ranks of subsets by at most one, so connectivity drops by at most two per step.

nodes.name: Vertical connectivity under perturbation
nodes.statement: Let $M, N$ be $\mathbb F$-represented matroids with $\mathrm{dist}(M,N) \leq k$. If $M$ is vertically $t$-connected, then $N$ is vertically $(t - 2k)$-connected.
assumptions: Let $M, N$ be $\mathbb F$-represented matroids with $\mathrm{dist}(M,N) \leq k$.
$M$ is vertically $t$-connected
conclusions: $N$ is vertically $(t - 2k)$-connected

There exists $k \in \mathbb Z^+$ such that every vertically $k$-connected matroid $M$ in $\mathcal{M}$ satisfies $\mathrm{dist}(M,N) \le k$ or $\mathrm{dist}(M^*,N) \le k$ for some $\mathbb F$-represented frame matroid $N$.

nodes.name: Moore bound for irregular graphs (girth bound)
nodes.statement: If $G$ is a graph with girth $g$ and average degree $\delta > 2$, then $g \le 4 + \tfrac{\log(|V(G)|)}{\log(\delta - 1)}$.
nodes.origin_citation: Alon, Hoory, Linial 2002; observed by Kashyap 2008
assumptions: $G$ is a graph with girth $g$ and average degree $\delta > 2$
conclusions: $g \le 4 + \tfrac{\log(|V(G)|)}{\log(\delta - 1)}$

nodes.name: Many short edge-disjoint cycles in dense graphs
nodes.statement: Let $t \in \mathbb Z^+$ and $\beta \in \mathbb R^+$. If $G$ is a graph with $|V(G)| = n\ge \max\left(\left(\frac{4t}{\beta\log(1+\beta)}\right)^2,(1+\beta)e^4\right)$ and $|E(G)| \ge (1+\beta)n$, then $G$ has a collection of $t$ pairwise edge-disjoint cycles, each of size at most $\tfrac{2\log n}{\log(1+\beta)}$.
assumptions: Let $t \in \mathbb Z^+$ and $\beta \in \mathbb R^+$.
$G$ is a graph with $|V(G)| = n\ge \max\left(\left(\frac{4t}{\beta\log(1+\beta)}\right)^2,(1+\beta)e^4\right)$ and $|E(G)| \ge (1+\beta)n$
conclusions: $G$ has a collection of $t$ pairwise edge-disjoint cycles, each of size at most $\tfrac{2\log n}{\log(1+\beta)}$
nodes.statement_short: A graph with $(1+\beta)n$ edges contains $t$ edge-disjoint cycles of length $O(\log n)$.
nodes.label: disjointcircuits

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.2
nodes.statement: Let $m = |E(G)|$ and $\alpha = 2(\log(1+\beta))^{-1}$. By choice of $n$ we have $\frac{t \alpha \log n}{n} < \tfrac{t \alpha}{\sqrt{n}} < \tfrac{1}{2}\beta$. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a maximal collection of pairwise disjoint cycles of $G$ such that $|E(C)| \le \alpha \log n$ for each $C \in \mathcal{C}$. Assume for a contradiction that $|\mathcal{C}| < t$; let $G' = G \!\setminus\! \cup \mathcal{C}$. We have $\tfrac{|E(G')|}{n} \ge \tfrac{m - t\alpha \log(n)}{n} \ge 1+\beta - \tfrac{t \alpha \log(n)}{n} > 1 + \tfrac{1}{2}\beta$, so the average degree $\delta'$ of $G'$ is at least $2 + \beta$. By maximality of $\mathcal{C}$, the graph $G'$ has girth $g' > \alpha \log (n)$, so Lemma~\ref{moore} gives \begin{align*} \alpha \log(n) &< 4 + \frac{\log(n)}{\log(\delta'-1)} \le 4 + \frac{\log(n)}{\log(1+\beta).} \end{align*} Rearranging gives $\log(n) < 4\log(1+\beta)$, contradicting $n \ge (1+\beta)e^4$.
nodes.statement_short: Contradiction: remove a maximal family of short disjoint cycles; the remainder is still dense with large girth, violating the Moore bound.

nodes.name: Dense frame matroids have small sets of large rank deficiency
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbb F$ be a finite field of order $q$, let $\beta \in \mathbb R^+$ and $t \in \mathbb Z^+$. Let $M$ be an $\mathbb F$-represented frame matroid with graph representation $(G,\Sigma)$, such that $G$ is connected. If $M$ satisfies \[r(M) \ge \max\left(|\mathbb F|,(2q-3)\beta^{-1}+1-q,\tfrac{1}{q-1}\left(\tfrac{4t}{\beta\log(1+\beta)}\right)^2,\tfrac{1+\beta}{q-1}e^4\right)\] and $|M| \ge (1+q\beta)r(M)$, then there is a set $X \subseteq E(M)$ such that $r_M(X) \le |X|-t$ and $|X| \le \tfrac{4 t\log r(M)}{\log(1+\beta)}$.
assumptions: Let $\mathbb F$ be a finite field of order $q$, let $\beta \in \mathbb R^+$ and $t \in \mathbb Z^+$.
Let $M$ be an $\mathbb F$-represented frame matroid with graph representation $(G,\Sigma)$, such that $G$ is connected.
$M$ satisfies \[r(M) \ge \max\left(|\mathbb F|,(2q-3)\beta^{-1}+1-q,\tfrac{1}{q-1}\left(\tfrac{4t}{\beta\log(1+\beta)}\right)^2,\tfrac{1+\beta}{q-1}e^4\right)\] and $|M| \ge (1+q\beta)r(M)$
conclusions: there is a set $X \subseteq E(M)$ such that $r_M(X) \le |X|-t$ and $|X| \le \tfrac{4 t\log r(M)}{\log(1+\beta)}$
nodes.statement_short: A dense connected frame matroid has a set of size $O(t\log r)$ whose rank is at least $t$ below its size.
nodes.label: framematroidrankdeficiency

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 5.3
nodes.statement: Let $A$ be an $\mathbb F$-frame matrix generating $M$ and let $(G,\Sigma)$ be a graph representation of $A$. Pick a spanning tree $T$ of $G$. By repeatedly resigning, we may assume that the edges of $T$ have sign $1$. Note that $|E(T)| \geq r(M) - 1$. Let $G^+$ denote the undirected graph with vertex set $V(G) \times \mathbb F^\times$ and edge set \begin{align*} & \{((\delta^{-}(e),\gamma),(\delta^{+}(e),\gamma)): e \in T, \gamma \in \mathbb F\}\\ \cup & \{((\delta^-(e), 1), (\delta^+(e), \mathrm{sign}(e))): e \in E(G)\setminus T\}; \end{align*} that is, we take $q-1$ copies of $T$, and each directed edge $(u,v)$ not in $T$ with sign $\gamma$ connects the copy of $T$ corresponding to $1$ with the copy of $T$ corresponding to $\gamma$. It is easy to check that each cycle of $G^+$, by projection onto the first coordinate, corresponds to either a balanced cycle of $(G,\Sigma)$, or a subgraph of $G$ of minimum degree 2 that is not a cycle. It follows from Proposition~\ref{bicycledependent} that every cycle of $G^+$ is dependent in $M$. Now, \begin{align*} |E(G^+)| & = (q-1)|E(T)| + |M| - |E(T)| \geq (q-2)(r(M) - 1) + |M|\\ & \ge (q-1)(1+\beta)r(M) + \beta r(M) - (q-2)\\ & \ge (1+\beta)|V(G^+)| - (q-1)(1+\beta) + \beta r(M) - q + 2\\ & \ge (1+\beta)|V(G^+)|, \end{align*} where we use $|E(T)| \geq r(M)-1$ first, $|M| \geq (1+q\beta)r(M)$ second, $|V(G^+)| \le (q-1)(r(M)+1)$ third, and $r(M) \ge (2q-3)\beta^{-1}+1-q$ last. By our lower bounds for $n = |V(G+)| \geq (q-1)r(M)$ and Lemma~\ref{disjointcircuits}, the graph $G^+$ contains $t$ pairwise disjoint cycles, each of size at most $\frac{2\log n}{\log(1+\beta)} \le \frac{4 \log r(M)}{\log(1+\beta)}$. Each of these cycles of $G$ is dependent in $M$, and it is thus easy to see that their union satisfies the result.
nodes.statement_short: Build the covering graph $G^+$ ($q-1$ copies of a spanning tree joined by non-tree arcs) whose cycles are dependent. It is dense enough for Lemma 5.2 to give $t$ short disjoint cycles.

nodes.name: Logarithmic girth near frame matroids
nodes.statement: Let $k \in \mathbb Z^+$, $\beta \in \mathbb R^+$, and $\mathbb F$ be a finite field. There exists $c \in \mathbb Z$ such that if $M$ is a rank-$r$ $\mathbb F$-represented matroid with $r > 2$ and $|M| \ge (1+ \beta)r$ and there is an $\mathbb F$-represented, connected frame matroid $N$ satisfying $\mathrm{dist}(M,N) \le k$, then $g(M) \le c \log r$.
assumptions: Let $k \in \mathbb Z^+$, $\beta \in \mathbb R^+$, and $\mathbb F$ be a finite field.
$M$ is a rank-$r$ $\mathbb F$-represented matroid with $r > 2$ and $|M| \ge (1+ \beta)r$
there is an $\mathbb F$-represented, connected frame matroid $N$ satisfying $\mathrm{dist}(M,N) \le k$
conclusions: There exists $c \in \mathbb Z$ such that
$g(M) \le c \log r$
nodes.statement_short: Dense matroids within bounded distance of a connected frame matroid have girth $O(\log r)$.
nodes.label: nearframe

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.4
nodes.statement: Let $\beta' = \tfrac{1}{2}\beta$ and $c \ge \max\Big((2q-3)\beta^{-1}+1-q$, $|\mathbb F|$, $\left(\tfrac{4(k+1)}{\beta'\log(1+\beta')}\right)^2$, $(1+\beta')e^4\Big)+k$ be an integer so that $4(k+1)\log(x+k) \le c \log(1+\beta')\log x$ for all $x \ge c$. Since $\beta' > 0$ we know that $M$ has a circuit, so $g(M) \le r+1$. If $r \le c-1$ then $g(M) \le r+1 \le c \le c \log r$, so the result holds; we may thus assume that $r \ge c$. Let $M^+$ be a matroid and $C,D \subseteq E(M^+)$ be sets of size at most $k$ so that $M^+ / C \!\setminus\! D = M$ and $M^+ / D \!\setminus\! C = N$. Since each $Y \subseteq E(M)$ satisfies $r_{M^+}(Y) \ge r_M(Y) \ge r_{M^+}(Y) - r_{M^+}(C) \ge r_{M^+}(Y) - k$ and a similar statement holds for $N$, we have $|r_M(Y) - r_{N}(Y)| \le k$ for each $Y \subseteq E(M)$. In particular, $r+k \ge r(N) \ge r - k \ge c-k$. By choice of $c$, Corollary~\ref{framematroidrankdeficiency} implies there is a set $X \subseteq E(N)$ with $r_{N}(X) \le |X|-(k+1)$ and $|X| \le \frac{4(k+1)\log(r(N))}{\log(1+\beta')} \le \tfrac{4(k+1)\log(r+k)}{\log(1+\beta')} \le c \log r$. Now $r_M(X) \le r_{N}(X) + k < |X|$, so $X$ contains a circuit of $M$ and therefore $g(M) \le c \log r$, as required.
nodes.statement_short: Ranks of $M$ and the nearby frame matroid $N$ differ by at most $k$; apply Corollary 5.3 to $N$ with $t=k+1$ to get a small dependent set in $M$.

nodes.name: Bounded girth near duals of frame matroids

There exists $c \in \mathbb Z$ so that, if $M$ is a nonempty $\mathbb F$-represented matroid such that $|M| \ge (1+\beta) r(M)$ and there is an $\mathbb F$-represented frame matroid $N$ with $\mathrm{dist}(M^*,N) \le k$ and connected graph, then $g(M) \le c$.
assumptions: Let $k \in \mathbb Z^+$, $\beta \in \mathbb R^+$, and $\mathbb F$ be a finite field.
$M$ is a nonempty $\mathbb F$-represented matroid such that $|M| \ge (1+\beta) r(M)$
there is an $\mathbb F$-represented frame matroid $N$ with $\mathrm{dist}(M^*,N) \le k$ and connected graph

$g(M) \le c$
nodes.statement_short: Dense matroids whose dual is near a connected frame matroid have girth bounded by a constant.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.5
nodes.statement: We may assume that $\beta \le 1$. Let $c = \lceil 12 \beta^{-1}(3k+1) \rceil$. If $|M| \le c$ then the result clearly holds, so we will assume otherwise. Let $M^+$ be a matroid and $C,D \subseteq E(M^+)$ be sets of size at most $k$ so that $M^+ / C \!\setminus\! D = M^*$ and $M^+ / D \!\setminus\! C = N$. As before, we have $|r_{M^*}(Y)-r_N(Y)| \le k$ for each $Y \subseteq E(M^*)$. Let $A$ be an $\mathbb F$-frame matrix generating $N$ with $r(N)$ rows (or $r(N)+1$ rows if $|\mathbb F| = 2$), and $(G,\Sigma)$ be an $\mathbb F^{\times}$-labelled graph associated with $N$. We have $|M^*| = |M| \ge (1+\beta)r(M) = (1+\beta)(|M^*| - r(M^*))$, giving $|M^*| \le (1 + \beta^{-1})r(M^*) \le 2\beta^{-1}r(M^*)$. Now $k \le r(M^*)-k \le r(N) \le |V(G)|+1 \le 2|V(G)|$, so \[|E(G)| = |N| = |M^*| \le 2\beta^{-1}(|V(G)|+k) \le 6\beta^{-1}|V(G)|.\] Therefore $G$ has average degree at most $12\beta^{-1}$. If $|V(G)| < 2(k+1)$, then $2(k+1)-1 \ge r(N) \ge r(M^*)-k$ so $r(M^*) \le 3k+1$. This gives $|M^*| \le 2\beta^{-1}(3k+1) < c$, a contradiction. Therefore $|V(G)| \ge 2(k+1)$, so there is a collection of $2(k+1)$ vertices of $G$ whose degrees sum to at most $12\beta^{-1}(k+1)$, so there is a set $F \subseteq E(G)$ such that $|F| \le 12\beta^{-1}(k+1) \le c$ and $r(N \!\setminus\! F) \le r(N)+1 - 2(k+1)$ (since $A$ has at most $r(N)+1$ rows and $A[E(N)-F]$ has at least $2(k+1)$ zero rows). Now \[r(M^* \!\setminus\! F) \le r(N \!\setminus\! F) + k \le r(N) - 2k -1 +k \le r(M^*) -1.\] Thus $F$ contains a cocircuit of $M^*$, which is a circuit of $M$, giving $g(M) \le c$.
nodes.statement_short: The frame graph of $N$ has bounded average degree, so deleting the edges at $2(k+1)$ low-degree vertices drops rank enough to give a small cocircuit of $M^*$.

nodes.name: Characterisation of asymptotically good minor-closed classes of represented matroids
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbb F$ be a finite field. If $\mathcal{M}$ is a minor-closed class of $\mathbb F$-represented matroids, then $\mathcal{M}$ is asymptotically good if and only if $\mathcal{M}$ contains all projective geometries over $\mathbb{F}_{\mathrm{prime}}$.

$\mathcal{M}$ is a minor-closed class of $\mathbb F$-represented matroids
conclusions: $\mathcal{M}$ is asymptotically good if and only if $\mathcal{M}$ contains all projective geometries over $\mathbb{F}_{\mathrm{prime}}$
nodes.statement_short: A minor-closed class of $\mathbb F$-represented matroids is asymptotically good iff it contains all projective geometries over the prime subfield.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6.1
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{M}$ contains all projective geometries over $\mathbb{F}_{\mathrm{prime}}$, then $\mathcal{M}$ contains all $\mathbb{F}_{\mathrm{prime}}$-represented matroids so is clearly asymptotically good. Suppose that $\mathcal{M}$ does not contain all projective geometries over $\mathbb{F}_{\mathrm{prime}}$ but is asymptotically good. By Theorem~\ref{big}, there is an integer $k$ so that every vertically $k$-connected matroid $M \in \mathcal{M}$ satisfies $\mathrm{dist}(M,N) \le k$ or $\mathrm{dist}(M^*,N) \le k$ for some $\mathbb F$-represented frame matroid $N$; moreover, $N$ is vertically $3$-connected by Lemma \ref{lem:connectedperturb}, so by Corollary \ref{cor:graphconn} we may assume the associated graph is connected. Let $\mathcal{M}_k$ denote the class of vertically $(2k+3)$-connected matroids in $M$. Note that every such matroid is also vertically $k$-connected. By Lemma~\ref{connreduction}, the class $\mathcal{M}_k$ is asymptotically good, so $\mathcal{M}_k$ contains an $(\alpha,\alpha)$-good sequence for some $\alpha \in (0,1)$. Let $\beta = (1-\alpha)^{-1}-1$ and let $c$ be the maximum of the two integers given by Lemmas~\ref{nearframe} and~\ref{nearcoframe} for $\mathbb F$, $\beta$ and $k$. Let $n_0$ be an integer so that $c \log n < \alpha n$ for all $n \ge n_0$. There is a matroid $M \in \mathcal{M}_k$ so that $|M| \ge n_0$, $d(M) = g(M^*) \ge \alpha|M|$ and $r(M) \ge \alpha|M|$. The last inequality gives $|M^*| \ge (1+\beta)r(M^*)$, so by Lemma~\ref{nearframe} or~\ref{nearcoframe} we have $d(M) \le c \log r(M^*) \le c \log |M^*| < \alpha |M^*|$, a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Contradiction: restrict to a highly connected asymptotically good subclass, apply the structure theorem, then the girth bounds of Lemmas 5.4/5.5 contradict linear distance.

nodes.name: Set $m$ and state and prove the nested connectivity claim
nodes.statement: Let $m = \max(m_1,m_2,8t\alpha^{-1})$. \begin{claim} For each $n \in \mathbb Z$ with $n \ge 2\beta^{-1}m$, the matroid $M_n$ is vertically $t$-connected. \end{claim} \begin{proof} Suppose for a contradiction that $n \ge 2\beta^{-1}m$ and $M = M_n$ is not vertically $t$-connected. Let $(X_1,X_2)$ be a partition of $E(M)$ with $r_M(X_1) + r_M(X_2) = r(M) + t' - 1$ with $t' < t$ and $r_M(X_1),r_M(X_2) \ge t'$. Let $N_1 = M/ X_2$ and $N_2 = M / X_1$. Note that $N_1,N_2 \in \mathcal{M}$ and that $r(N_i) = r(M)-r_M(X_{3-i}) > r(M)-t+1$, so $r(N_1) + r(N_2) > r(M)-2t$. Since every cocircuit of $N_1$ or $N_2$ is a cocircuit of $M$, we have $g(M^*) \le \min(g(N_1^*),g(N_2^*))$.We have \[ \beta|M| \le g(M^*) \le \min(g(N_1^*),g(N_2^*)) \le \tfrac{1}{2}(g(N_1^*) + g(N_2^*))\] and, since $|M| = |N_1| + |N_2|$, we have either $g(N_1^*) \ge 2\beta|N_1|$ or $g(N_2^*) \ge 2\beta|N_2|$. We may assume that the first case holds. Since each of $X_1$ and $X_2$ contains a cocircuit of $M$, we have $|N_i| = |X_i| \ge g(M^*) \ge \beta|M| \ge m$ for each $i \in \{1,2\}$. Since $|N_1| + |N_2| = |M|$, this implies that $|N_1| \ge \tfrac{\beta}{1-\beta}|N_2|$. Moreover, $m \ge m_1$ gives $r(N_1) < \tfrac{1}{2}\alpha|N_1|$. We have \begin{align*} \alpha|M| &\le r(M) \\ &< r(N_1) + r(N_2) + 2t\\ &< \tfrac{1}{2}\alpha|N_1| + r(N_2) + 2t\\ &\le \tfrac{3}{4}\alpha|N_1| + r(N_2), \end{align*} Where the last line uses $\tfrac{1}{4}\alpha|N_1| \ge \tfrac{1}{4}\alpha m \ge 2t$. From this and $|M| = |N_1|+|N_2|$ we get \begin{align*} r(N_2) &\ge \tfrac{1}{4}\alpha|N_1| + \alpha|N_2|\\ &= \alpha\left(1 + \delta \right)|N_2| \end{align*} Now $|N_2| \ge m \ge m_2$ so $g(N_2^*) < \beta |N_2|$ by choice of $m_2$. However $g(M^*) \le g(N_2^*)$ and $\beta|N_2| < \beta|M|$, so $g(M^*) < \beta|M|$, contradicting the definition of $M$. \end{proof}

nodes.name: Rank and cogirth bounds
nodes.statement: Note that $N_1,N_2 \in \mathcal{M}$ and that $r(N_i) = r(M)-r_M(X_{3-i}) > r(M)-t+1$, so $r(N_1) + r(N_2) > r(M)-2t$. Since every cocircuit of $N_1$ or $N_2$ is a cocircuit of $M$, we have $g(M^*) \le \min(g(N_1^*),g(N_2^*))$.We have \[ \beta|M| \le g(M^*) \le \min(g(N_1^*),g(N_2^*)) \le \tfrac{1}{2}(g(N_1^*) + g(N_2^*))\] and, since $|M| = |N_1| + |N_2|$, we have either $g(N_1^*) \ge 2\beta|N_1|$ or $g(N_2^*) \ge 2\beta|N_2|$. We may assume that the first case holds.
nodes.statement_short: Rank and cogirth bounds; one side has cogirth at least $2\beta|N_1|$

nodes.name: Both sides are large
nodes.statement: Since each of $X_1$ and $X_2$ contains a cocircuit of $M$, we have $|N_i| = |X_i| \ge g(M^*) \ge \beta|M| \ge m$ for each $i \in \{1,2\}$. Since $|N_1| + |N_2| = |M|$, this implies that $|N_1| \ge \tfrac{\beta}{1-\beta}|N_2|$. Moreover, $m \ge m_1$ gives $r(N_1) < \tfrac{1}{2}\alpha|N_1|$. We have \begin{align*} \alpha|M| &\le r(M) \\ &< r(N_1) + r(N_2) + 2t\\ &< \tfrac{1}{2}\alpha|N_1| + r(N_2) + 2t\\ &\le \tfrac{3}{4}\alpha|N_1| + r(N_2), \end{align*} Where the last line uses $\tfrac{1}{4}\alpha|N_1| \ge \tfrac{1}{4}\alpha m \ge 2t$. From this and $|M| = |N_1|+|N_2|$ we get \begin{align*} r(N_2) &\ge \tfrac{1}{4}\alpha|N_1| + \alpha|N_2|\\ &= \alpha\left(1 + \delta \right)|N_2| \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Both sides are large; rank bounds give $r(N_2)\ge\alpha(1+\delta)|N_2|$

nodes.name: Choice of $m_2$ forces small cogirth, a contradiction
nodes.statement: Now $|N_2| \ge m \ge m_2$ so $g(N_2^*) < \beta |N_2|$ by choice of $m_2$. However $g(M^*) \le g(N_2^*)$ and $\beta|N_2| < \beta|M|$, so $g(M^*) < \beta|M|$, contradicting the definition of $M$.
nodes.statement_short: Choice of $m_2$ forces small cogirth, a contradiction

nodes.name: Set $m,\alpha$ and bound $t\alpha\log n/n$
nodes.statement: Let $m = |E(G)|$ and $\alpha = 2(\log(1+\beta))^{-1}$. By choice of $n$ we have $\frac{t \alpha \log n}{n} < \tfrac{t \alpha}{\sqrt{n}} < \tfrac{1}{2}\beta$.
nodes.statement_short: Set $m,\alpha$ and bound $t\alpha\log n/n$

nodes.name: Take a maximal family of short disjoint cycles
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a maximal collection of pairwise disjoint cycles of $G$ such that $|E(C)| \le \alpha \log n$ for each $C \in \mathcal{C}$. Assume for a contradiction that $|\mathcal{C}| < t$; let $G' = G \!\setminus\! \cup \mathcal{C}$.
nodes.statement_short: Take a maximal family of short disjoint cycles; assume fewer than $t$

nodes.name: $G'$ still has average degree at least $2+\beta$
nodes.statement: We have $\tfrac{|E(G')|}{n} \ge \tfrac{m - t\alpha \log(n)}{n} \ge 1+\beta - \tfrac{t \alpha \log(n)}{n} > 1 + \tfrac{1}{2}\beta$, so the average degree $\delta'$ of $G'$ is at least $2 + \beta$.
nodes.statement_short: $G'$ still has average degree at least $2+\beta$

nodes.name: Apply the Moore bound to $G'$
nodes.statement: By maximality of $\mathcal{C}$, the graph $G'$ has girth $g' > \alpha \log (n)$, so Lemma~\ref{moore} gives \begin{align*} \alpha \log(n) &< 4 + \frac{\log(n)}{\log(\delta'-1)} \le 4 + \frac{\log(n)}{\log(1+\beta).} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the Moore bound to $G'$

nodes.name: Rearrange to contradict the lower bound on $n$
nodes.statement: Rearranging gives $\log(n) < 4\log(1+\beta)$, contradicting $n \ge (1+\beta)e^4$.
nodes.statement_short: Rearrange to contradict the lower bound on $n$

nodes.name: Choose a graph representation and spanning tree
nodes.statement: Let $A$ be an $\mathbb F$-frame matrix generating $M$ and let $(G,\Sigma)$ be a graph representation of $A$. Pick a spanning tree $T$ of $G$. By repeatedly resigning, we may assume that the edges of $T$ have sign $1$. Note that $|E(T)| \geq r(M) - 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose a graph representation and spanning tree; resign tree edges to 1

nodes.name: Construct covering graph $G^+$
nodes.statement: Let $G^+$ denote the undirected graph with vertex set $V(G) \times \mathbb F^\times$ and edge set \begin{align*} & \{((\delta^{-}(e),\gamma),(\delta^{+}(e),\gamma)): e \in T, \gamma \in \mathbb F\}\\ \cup & \{((\delta^-(e), 1), (\delta^+(e), \mathrm{sign}(e))): e \in E(G)\setminus T\}; \end{align*} that is, we take $q-1$ copies of $T$, and each directed edge $(u,v)$ not in $T$ with sign $\gamma$ connects the copy of $T$ corresponding to $1$ with the copy of $T$ corresponding to $\gamma$. It is easy to check that each cycle of $G^+$, by projection onto the first coordinate, corresponds to either a balanced cycle of $(G,\Sigma)$, or a subgraph of $G$ of minimum degree 2 that is not a cycle.
nodes.statement_short: Construct covering graph $G^+$; its cycles project to balanced cycles or bicycles

nodes.name: Proposition 2.2: every cycle of $G^+$ is dependent
nodes.statement: It follows from Proposition~\ref{bicycledependent} that every cycle of $G^+$ is dependent in $M$.
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 2.2: every cycle of $G^+$ is dependent

nodes.name: Show $|E(G^+)|\ge(1+\beta)|V(G^+)|$
nodes.statement: Now, \begin{align*} |E(G^+)| & = (q-1)|E(T)| + |M| - |E(T)| \geq (q-2)(r(M) - 1) + |M|\\ & \ge (q-1)(1+\beta)r(M) + \beta r(M) - (q-2)\\ & \ge (1+\beta)|V(G^+)| - (q-1)(1+\beta) + \beta r(M) - q + 2\\ & \ge (1+\beta)|V(G^+)|, \end{align*} where we use $|E(T)| \geq r(M)-1$ first, $|M| \geq (1+q\beta)r(M)$ second, $|V(G^+)| \le (q-1)(r(M)+1)$ third, and $r(M) \ge (2q-3)\beta^{-1}+1-q$ last.
nodes.statement_short: Show $|E(G^+)|\ge(1+\beta)|V(G^+)|$

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 5.2 to $G^+$
nodes.statement: By our lower bounds for $n = |V(G+)| \geq (q-1)r(M)$ and Lemma~\ref{disjointcircuits}, the graph $G^+$ contains $t$ pairwise disjoint cycles, each of size at most $\frac{2\log n}{\log(1+\beta)} \le \frac{4 \log r(M)}{\log(1+\beta)}$. Each of these cycles of $G$ is dependent in $M$, and it is thus easy to see that their union satisfies the result.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 5.2 to $G^+$; union of the $t$ short cycles works

nodes.name: Choose $\beta'$ and constant $c$
nodes.statement: Let $\beta' = \tfrac{1}{2}\beta$ and $c \ge \max\Big((2q-3)\beta^{-1}+1-q$, $|\mathbb F|$, $\left(\tfrac{4(k+1)}{\beta'\log(1+\beta')}\right)^2$, $(1+\beta')e^4\Big)+k$ be an integer so that $4(k+1)\log(x+k) \le c \log(1+\beta')\log x$ for all $x \ge c$. Since $\beta' > 0$ we know that $M$ has a circuit, so $g(M) \le r+1$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose $\beta'$ and constant $c$; note $g(M)\le r+1$

nodes.name: Small rank is trivial
nodes.statement: If $r \le c-1$ then $g(M) \le r+1 \le c \le c \log r$, so the result holds; we may thus assume that $r \ge c$.
nodes.statement_short: Small rank is trivial; assume $r\ge c$

nodes.name: Ranks in $M$ and $N$ differ by at most $k$
nodes.statement: Let $M^+$ be a matroid and $C,D \subseteq E(M^+)$ be sets of size at most $k$ so that $M^+ / C \!\setminus\! D = M$ and $M^+ / D \!\setminus\! C = N$. Since each $Y \subseteq E(M)$ satisfies $r_{M^+}(Y) \ge r_M(Y) \ge r_{M^+}(Y) - r_{M^+}(C) \ge r_{M^+}(Y) - k$ and a similar statement holds for $N$, we have $|r_M(Y) - r_{N}(Y)| \le k$ for each $Y \subseteq E(M)$. In particular, $r+k \ge r(N) \ge r - k \ge c-k$.
nodes.statement_short: Ranks in $M$ and $N$ differ by at most $k$

nodes.name: Corollary 5.3 gives a small set of rank deficiency $k+1$ in
nodes.statement: By choice of $c$, Corollary~\ref{framematroidrankdeficiency} implies there is a set $X \subseteq E(N)$ with $r_{N}(X) \le |X|-(k+1)$ and $|X| \le \frac{4(k+1)\log(r(N))}{\log(1+\beta')} \le \tfrac{4(k+1)\log(r+k)}{\log(1+\beta')} \le c \log r$.
nodes.statement_short: Corollary 5.3 gives a small set of rank deficiency $k+1$ in $N$

nodes.name: The set is dependent in $M$, giving $g(M)\le c\log r$
nodes.statement: Now $r_M(X) \le r_{N}(X) + k < |X|$, so $X$ contains a circuit of $M$ and therefore $g(M) \le c \log r$, as required.
nodes.statement_short: The set is dependent in $M$, giving $g(M)\le c\log r$

nodes.name: WLOG $\beta\le1$ and $|M|>c$
nodes.statement: We may assume that $\beta \le 1$. Let $c = \lceil 12 \beta^{-1}(3k+1) \rceil$. If $|M| \le c$ then the result clearly holds, so we will assume otherwise. Let $M^+$ be a matroid and $C,D \subseteq E(M^+)$ be sets of size at most $k$ so that $M^+ / C \!\setminus\! D = M^*$ and $M^+ / D \!\setminus\! C = N$. As before, we have $|r_{M^*}(Y)-r_N(Y)| \le k$ for each $Y \subseteq E(M^*)$.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG $\beta\le1$ and $|M|>c$; ranks of $M^*$ and $N$ differ by at most $k$

nodes.name: Take a frame representation of $N$
nodes.statement: Let $A$ be an $\mathbb F$-frame matrix generating $N$ with $r(N)$ rows (or $r(N)+1$ rows if $|\mathbb F| = 2$), and $(G,\Sigma)$ be an $\mathbb F^{\times}$-labelled graph associated with $N$. We have $|M^*| = |M| \ge (1+\beta)r(M) = (1+\beta)(|M^*| - r(M^*))$, giving $|M^*| \le (1 + \beta^{-1})r(M^*) \le 2\beta^{-1}r(M^*)$.
nodes.statement_short: Take a frame representation of $N$; bound $|M^*|$ by $2\beta^{-1}r(M^*)$

nodes.name: The graph of $N$ has bounded average degree
nodes.statement: Now $k \le r(M^*)-k \le r(N) \le |V(G)|+1 \le 2|V(G)|$, so \[|E(G)| = |N| = |M^*| \le 2\beta^{-1}(|V(G)|+k) \le 6\beta^{-1}|V(G)|.\] Therefore $G$ has average degree at most $12\beta^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_short: The graph of $N$ has bounded average degree

nodes.name: Rule out graphs with fewer than $2(k+1)$ vertices
nodes.statement: If $|V(G)| < 2(k+1)$, then $2(k+1)-1 \ge r(N) \ge r(M^*)-k$ so $r(M^*) \le 3k+1$. This gives $|M^*| \le 2\beta^{-1}(3k+1) < c$, a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Rule out graphs with fewer than $2(k+1)$ vertices

nodes.name: Delete edges at $2(k+1)$ low-degree vertices to drop rank of
nodes.statement: Therefore $|V(G)| \ge 2(k+1)$, so there is a collection of $2(k+1)$ vertices of $G$ whose degrees sum to at most $12\beta^{-1}(k+1)$, so there is a set $F \subseteq E(G)$ such that $|F| \le 12\beta^{-1}(k+1) \le c$ and $r(N \!\setminus\! F) \le r(N)+1 - 2(k+1)$ (since $A$ has at most $r(N)+1$ rows and $A[E(N)-F]$ has at least $2(k+1)$ zero rows).
nodes.statement_short: Delete edges at $2(k+1)$ low-degree vertices to drop rank of $N$

nodes.name: $F$ contains a cocircuit of $M^*$, a circuit of $M$
nodes.statement: Now \[r(M^* \!\setminus\! F) \le r(N \!\setminus\! F) + k \le r(N) - 2k -1 +k \le r(M^*) -1.\] Thus $F$ contains a cocircuit of $M^*$, which is a circuit of $M$, giving $g(M) \le c$.
nodes.statement_short: $F$ contains a cocircuit of $M^*$, a circuit of $M$

nodes.name: Easy direction: containing all projective geometries
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{M}$ contains all projective geometries over $\mathbb{F}_{\mathrm{prime}}$, then $\mathcal{M}$ contains all $\mathbb{F}_{\mathrm{prime}}$-represented matroids so is clearly asymptotically good.
nodes.statement_short: Easy direction: containing all projective geometries

nodes.name: Assume the class excludes a projective geometry but is asymp
nodes.statement: Suppose that $\mathcal{M}$ does not contain all projective geometries over $\mathbb{F}_{\mathrm{prime}}$ but is asymptotically good.
nodes.statement_short: Assume the class excludes a projective geometry but is asymptotically good

nodes.name: Apply the structure theorem and connectivity lemmas
nodes.statement: By Theorem~\ref{big}, there is an integer $k$ so that every vertically $k$-connected matroid $M \in \mathcal{M}$ satisfies $\mathrm{dist}(M,N) \le k$ or $\mathrm{dist}(M^*,N) \le k$ for some $\mathbb F$-represented frame matroid $N$; moreover, $N$ is vertically $3$-connected by Lemma \ref{lem:connectedperturb}, so by Corollary \ref{cor:graphconn} we may assume the associated graph is connected.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the structure theorem and connectivity lemmas

nodes.name: Define $\mathcal{M}_k$ of vertically $(2k+3)$-connected memb
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{M}_k$ denote the class of vertically $(2k+3)$-connected matroids in $M$. Note that every such matroid is also vertically $k$-connected.
nodes.statement_short: Define $\mathcal{M}_k$ of vertically $(2k+3)$-connected members

nodes.name: Lemma 3.1: $\mathcal{M}_k$ is asymptotically good
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{connreduction}, the class $\mathcal{M}_k$ is asymptotically good, so $\mathcal{M}_k$ contains an $(\alpha,\alpha)$-good sequence for some $\alpha \in (0,1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.1: $\mathcal{M}_k$ is asymptotically good

nodes.name: Fix $\beta$, the constant $c$ from Lemmas 5.4/5.5, and $n_0$
nodes.statement: Let $\beta = (1-\alpha)^{-1}-1$ and let $c$ be the maximum of the two integers given by Lemmas~\ref{nearframe} and~\ref{nearcoframe} for $\mathbb F$, $\beta$ and $k$. Let $n_0$ be an integer so that $c \log n < \alpha n$ for all $n \ge n_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix $\beta$, the constant $c$ from Lemmas 5.4/5.5, and $n_0$

nodes.name: Pick a large good matroid $M$ in $\mathcal{M}_k$
nodes.statement: There is a matroid $M \in \mathcal{M}_k$ so that $|M| \ge n_0$, $d(M) = g(M^*) \ge \alpha|M|$ and $r(M) \ge \alpha|M|$.
nodes.statement_short: Pick a large good matroid $M$ in $\mathcal{M}_k$

nodes.name: Lemmas 5.4/5.5 bound $d(M)$ logarithmically, contradicting l
nodes.statement: The last inequality gives $|M^*| \ge (1+\beta)r(M^*)$, so by Lemma~\ref{nearframe} or~\ref{nearcoframe} we have $d(M) \le c \log r(M^*) \le c \log |M^*| < \alpha |M^*|$, a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Lemmas 5.4/5.5 bound $d(M)$ logarithmically, contradicting linear distance
